candidate.title: TAmC-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned TAmC-Seq (Tet-assisted 5-methylcytosine sequencing) schematic: the middle row from DNA containing 5mC/5hmC through protective glucosylation, Tet oxidation, azide-glucose labelling, biotinylation, and streptavidin capture/DTT release to enriched DNA. The card title and the matching collection-page heading/caption identify this row as the target. Aba-seq above and fC-Seal below are separate neighboring catalogue workflows; the clipped JBP1-seq row and right-edge chemistry are also context, not alternatives or branches of TAmC-Seq. The graph preserves the two drawn chemical transformations of oxidation and azide-glucosylation while identifying their coupled one-pot implementation in Zhang et al. 2013. The diagram ends before library preparation/sequencing; the paper supplies the readout interface, not extra drawn operations.

operations.label: βGT / Glucosylation
operations.description: β-GT adds regular glucose to endogenous 5hmC on the input DNA, producing protected g5hmC while leaving original 5mC available for conversion.
operations.mechanism: T4 bacteriophage β-glucosyltransferase transfers regular glucose from UDP-glucose to 5hmC; the protected product is not further oxidized or labelled in the reported scheme.
operations.information_effect: Distinguishes pre-existing 5hmC from 5hmC subsequently generated from 5mC, so later affinity tags are intended to report original 5mC.

operations.label: TET / Oxidation
operations.description: Tet oxidation changes original 5mC into new 5hmC on the already protected DNA. The original g5hmC remains protected. The oxidized-site label 5cmC in the drawing is interpreted as 5hmC from the primary paper.
operations.mechanism: The paper identifies the catalyst as the mouse Tet1 catalytic domain (mTet1). This transformation is coupled to β-GT trapping in one pot, which limits further oxidation to 5fC/5caC; the drawn arrow is a conceptual reaction boundary.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the identity of originally methylated positions into a labelable hydroxymethyl intermediate on the same DNA.

operations.label: βGT-catalyzed UDP-6-N3 glucosylation
operations.description: β-GT transfers 6-N3-glucose to newly generated 5hmC, producing azide-bearing N3-5gmC on DNA derived from original 5mC. Existing regular-glucose-protected 5hmC is retained without the new tag.
operations.mechanism: UDP-6-N3-glucose is the modified glucose donor; β-GT immediately traps the Tet-generated 5hmC in the reported one-pot mTet1/β-GT implementation. The separate drawing denotes this chemical transformation, not a required separate incubation.
operations.information_effect: Introduces an azide handle on the same genomic DNA carrier at sites that were originally 5mC, preserving distinction from protected endogenous 5hmC.

operations.label: Biotinylation
operations.description: Biotin is attached through the azide handle of the modified glucose, converting azide-labelled DNA into affinity-capture-compatible DNA. The source depicts an S-S-containing biotin linkage.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper specifies Huisgen cycloaddition (click) chemistry for installing the biotin tag through the azide.
operations.information_effect: Converts the chemical record of original 5mC into a physical affinity handle carried by genomic DNA fragments.

operations.label: Streptavidin pulldown and DTT cleavage
operations.description: Streptavidin affinity capture selects the biotin-tagged DNA; DTT cleavage releases enriched DNA, shown as the terminal DNA line. Capture and release are retained as the single combined block drawn.
operations.mechanism: Biotin/streptavidin binding provides affinity selection. The depicted S-S biotin linkage together with the DTT-cleavage caption supports reductive linker cleavage as the release mechanism, not cleavage of the DNA backbone. The exact residual tag is not drawn.
operations.information_effect: The selected carrier is genomic DNA, enriched for fragments containing original 5mC. The paper-supported downstream Illumina library sequences these fragments to map regional methylation enrichment; selection alone does not establish perfect specificity or single-base methylation calls.

corrections.primary_statement: The reported genomic-DNA TAmC-Seq implementation uses a one-pot mTet1/β-GT reaction: newly generated 5hmC is immediately trapped with 6-N3-glucose, limiting further oxidation to 5fC and 5caC.
